title: Hopf Modules, Coinvariants, and the Fundamental Theorem

items.title: Right-right Hopf modules and coinvariants
items.statement: Over a field k and a Hopf algebra H, define a right-right Hopf module to be a right H-module M, right H-comodule rho:M->M tensor H, and compatibility rho(mh)=sum m_0 h_1 tensor m_1 h_2. Define M^coH={m:rho(m)=m tensor 1}; morphisms preserve both structures.
items.strategy: Definition; coinvariants are kernel-defined, with their subspace property proved by a separate local lemma.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, Theorem 2.1
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Definition 3.34

items.title: The coinvariants of a right-right Hopf module form a subspace
items.statement: For every right-right Hopf module M, M^coH={m in M:rho(m)=m tensor 1} is a k-linear subspace of M.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, coinvariants preceding Theorem 2.1
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Definition 3.37

items.title: The free right-right Hopf module on a vector space
items.statement: For any k-vector space V and Hopf algebra H, V tensor H has right action (v tensor h)g=v tensor hg and right coaction rho(v tensor h)=sum (v tensor h_1) tensor h_2, making it a right-right Hopf module.
items.strategy: Check the module, comodule, and compatibility axioms on elementary tensors.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, trivial Hopf modules
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Example 3.36

items.title: The coinvariant projection of a right-right Hopf module
items.statement: For a right-right Hopf module, P(m)=sum m_0 S(m_1) is a linear map M->M^coH, restricts to the identity on M^coH, and is therefore an idempotent projection. Its proof uses the antipode's anti-comultiplication identity but never S^{-1}.
items.strategy: Compute the coaction of P(m), using the Hopf-module compatibility, anti-comultiplicativity, and the two antipode identities.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, proof of Theorem 2.1
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, proof of Theorem 3.38, Step 1

items.title: The fundamental theorem of right-right Hopf modules
items.statement: For every right-right Hopf module M over a Hopf algebra H over a field k, alpha:M^coH tensor H->M, n tensor h|->nh, is an isomorphism of right-right Hopf modules, with inverse beta(m)=sum P(m_0) tensor m_1. No bijectivity hypothesis on the antipode is assumed.
items.strategy: Construct alpha and beta, show beta lands in the tensor product with the coinvariant subspace by applying P tensor id, compute both composites, and verify the structure maps.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, Theorem 2.1 and complete proof
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Theorem 3.38 and complete proof

items.title: Coinvariants of a free right-right Hopf module
items.statement: For any k-vector space V, the coinvariants of the free Hopf module V tensor H, with coaction on the H factor, are exactly V tensor 1, canonically isomorphic to V via v|->v tensor 1.
items.strategy: Use the counit map id_V tensor epsilon on an arbitrary coinvariant tensor; no basis or choice principle is needed.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, trivial Hopf modules and Theorem 2.1
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Theorem 3.38

items.title: Right-right Hopf modules are equivalent to vector spaces
items.statement: The coinvariants functor from right-right Hopf modules over H to k-vector spaces and the free Hopf module functor V|->V tensor H are inverse equivalences, with the natural unit v|->v tensor 1 and counit n tensor h|->nh.
items.strategy: Define both functors on objects and morphisms, prove the unit and counit are natural isomorphisms, and verify the triangle identities on elementary tensors and coinvariants.

references.title: Hans-Juergen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf Algebras, notes by Sonia Natale, section 2, Theorem 2.1
D. S. Drogalski, Chapter 3: Hopf Algebras, section 3.6, Theorem 3.38 and Corollary 3.39

title: Hopf Modules, Coinvariants, and the Fundamental Theorem — Examples

items.title: The regular Hopf module and its projection
items.statement: For H with its regular right action and right coaction Delta, the coinvariants are k1, the projection is h|->epsilon(h)1, and the theorem's decomposition is the canonical k tensor H isomorphism.
items.strategy: Direct calculation from the antipode and counit identities.

items.title: The free Hopf module over a group algebra
items.statement: For any group G, field k and k-vector space V, compute the action, coaction, coinvariants, projection and inverse decomposition on V tensor kG.
items.strategy: Verify on basis group elements and extend each linear identity to finite sums.

items.title: The free Hopf module over the polynomial Hopf algebra
items.statement: For the primitive polynomial Hopf algebra k[x], compute the coaction, coinvariants, projection and inverse decomposition on V tensor k[x] in every characteristic.
items.strategy: Expand Delta(x^n) by the binomial theorem and evaluate the alternating binomial sum for the projection.

items.title: A module and comodule need not satisfy Hopf compatibility
items.statement: The assertion that any right module and right comodule on the same vector space automatically form a right-right Hopf module is false.
items.strategy: Use the trivial action and a nontrivial group-like coaction over the group algebra of C2.
